learning_objectives.outcome: The learner can identify the structure of an HTML document and explain the role of the <html>, <head>, and <body> elements
learning_objectives.verifiable_by: Given a labeled diagram of an HTML document skeleton, the learner can match each section (doctype, html, head, body) with its correct purpose

learning_objectives.outcome: The learner can write HTML elements with attributes for headings, paragraphs, links, and images
learning_objectives.verifiable_by: Given a content specification ('a link to example.com that opens in a new tab'), the learner writes the correct anchor tag with the href and target attributes

learning_objectives.outcome: The learner can construct a valid, minimal HTML page from scratch using proper nesting and indentation
learning_objectives.verifiable_by: The learner writes a complete .html file that renders a heading, a paragraph, an image, and a link — all correctly nested inside the body element, and verifiable via browser preview

learner_transformation: Goes from having no idea how web pages are built to being able to read, understand, and write a simple structured HTML document using text elements, links, and images — confidently distinguishing between content and the tags that wrap it.

key_insights.insight: HTML is not a programming language — it's a markup language that describes and structures content.
key_insights.why_it_matters: This reframe prevents beginners from feeling overwhelmed by 'coding.' They can relax and focus on wrapping content in the right tags rather than worrying about logic, variables, or control flow.

key_insights.insight: Every piece of content lives between an opening and closing tag (or inside a self-closing one) — and getting the nesting right is what gives a page structure.
key_insights.why_it_matters: Beginners often forget closing tags or mis-nest elements. Internalizing the 'open—content—close' pattern early prevents the most common HTML bugs and builds intuition for how browsers interpret code.

key_insights.insight: Attributes are the 'settings' on an HTML element — without them, an image has no source and a link has no destination.
key_insights.why_it_matters: This mental model helps learners remember that tags like or need extra instructions (src, href) to work, and that attributes are always written inside the opening tag as name-value pairs.

budget_notes: Duration was not specified by the user. I derived target_duration_minutes = 30 based on scope analysis: HTML fundamentals for absolute beginners needs enough time to establish the markup concept, syntax patterns, and a simple build exercise. Three learning objectives fit the 20–40 min heuristic cleanly (2–3 objectives). No tension detected — scope is realistic, audience starting point matches the outcome level, and goal uses 'learn fundamentals' (not mastery language).
